answer: A copper stake escrow makes each identity pay to exist: an agent locks a small copper-denominated deposit in a shared vault before it can trade, and the vault only releases it after a season of honest work. A Sybil farmer spawning thousands of sock-puppet agents must fund every one of them, so the attack cost grows linearly while its payoff stays flat — like saffron, where each thread must be picked by hand, identity here is expensive to grow and cheap to verify, which starves mass fakery at the root.
